newsitem.title: UK: Tanker charter rates mostly stable, W.Africa firm.
newsitem.headline: Tanker charter rates mostly stable, W.Africa firm.

text.p: Crude oil tanker chartering rates were mostly stable in thin activity with fresh fixings for larger cargoes in most regions limited, brokers said.
Rates for transatlantic voyages from West Africa continued firm with suitable tonnage for the U.S. market in thin supply.
"Ther are only about 10 (Modern) cargoes left to the end of the month -- that's pretty poor," one broker said.

No new VLCC fixings from West Africa to the U.S. Gulf were reported but a Suezmax cargo with Atlantic coast options was fixed at W100 and W102.5 respectively, indicating the market around nine points higher.
A 140kt cargo from West Africa to UKC took W97.5 while an Austrian refiner paid W87.50 for a million barrels into Trieste.

Inter UK/Cont fixings were fairly brisk today. Rates firmed a couple of points to W102.5 with several Aframax cargoes fixed into U.K. refiners at between W100 and W105 while UKC options were done at W102.5.
Transatlantic business from the North Sea remained thin with rates for VLCCs pegged around W62.5 and Suezmax around W80.
Western hemisphere play continued to focus on East coast Mexico/USG fixings with 70kt cargoes valued around W130.
A spanish refiner fixed a 140,000 tonne Mexican cargo to Spain at W55 and an Italian refiner fixed a veseel for 74.5kt from Puerto Miranda to Gela at W120.
Medeast Gulf activity was also thinner today. No new fixings for Japan were reported but traders valued the market steady around W62.5 in line with the last trade on Monday at W62.75.
South Korea continued to draw VLCC tonnage with four cargoes seen booked, one talking at the firmer rate of W59.5.
Cross Mediterranean activity was slower and rates for Aframax cargoes slipped 2-1/2 points to W97.50. A cargo with UKC-Med options was fixed from Novorossiisk at the same level.
